root.name: Indian Defense: Colle System, King's Indian Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. e3 Bg7 4. Bd3 d6

overview: White plays the Colle set-up with e3, Bd3, O-O and Nbd2 against Black's King's Indian fianchetto, aiming for an e4 break with c3 or the c4 and Qe2 options. Black plays ...O-O and ...c5 or ...e5 to challenge d4, and the game is a plan-based fight with no heavy theory. The set-up is easy to play but gives Black a comfortable game.

white_ideas.idea: O-O, Nbd2 and c3 then e4 to build a pawn centre.
Qe2 and e4, or Ne5 and f4 for kingside play.

black_ideas.idea: ...O-O and ...c5 or ...e5 to strike d4 before White gets e4.

typical_structures.structure: White pawns on d4/e3/c3 with a bishop on d3 against a King's Indian fianchetto.

character.notes: Quiet developing set-up, low risk for White; Black has a comfortable game.

approach.notes: The Colle is a system: same set-up against many defences.

level.notes: Clear plans, little to memorise; a coach would hand it to a new player.

structure.reason: Centre tension d4 against ...e5 or ...c5 undecided.
